The strict condition $H^0$ and the relaxed condition $H^0\oplus H^1[-1]$ are mutually dual. All four inclusions can be equipped with compatible integral duality triangles.
  - Explanation: Inert good primes approaching complex conjugation yield a split local complex with explicit finite and singular coordinates, integral isotropic planes, and compatible strict–relaxed duality triangles.
- **claim-uniform-heegner-derivative-descent** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-h-derivative-classes)): Suppose that the finite ring-class transfers are performed before retaining their target cycles and witnesses as in Lemma <a href="#rl:finite-limits" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="rl:finite-limits">74</a>. There is one integer $L\ne0$, depending on the fixed curve, parametrization and fixed local types, such that the classes obtained from the Heegner derivatives of $L$ times the point satisfy, for every finite switched set $I$, $$P_I\in H^1(C_I),\qquad f(P_{I\cup\{\ell\}})=0,\qquad s(P_{I\cup\{\ell\}})=C_\tau f(P_I). \label{eq:h:finite-singular}$$ The same $L$ works for every number of active and derivative primes. The previously imposed singular conditions are retained.
  - Explanation: One fixed multiplier suffices for complete-conductor descent and bad-prime Kummer conditions. The derivative switch kills the new finite coordinate and identifies the singular coordinate with the conjugated old finite coordinate.
- **claim-switch-preserves-determinant-valuation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-h-determinant-switch)): Let $\mathcal O$ be a height-one discrete valuation ring at which the complexes and switching conditions are self-dual. Suppose the generic Selmer group for a set $I$ has rank one and is spanned by $P_I$, and $v_0=f(P_I)$ is nonzero at the next derivative prime. Then the switched generic group has rank one and is spanned by $P_{I\cup\{l\}}$, and $$\label{eq:h:switch-equality} v_{\mathcal O}(u_I)=v_{\mathcal O}(u_{I\cup\{l\}}).$$ This assertion does not require a primitive localization in either integral plane.
  - Explanation: A nonzero next finite localization preserves generic rank one and determinant valuation after switching, even when integral localizations are not primitive.
- **claim-height-one-rank-reduction** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-h-height-one-reduction)): Suppose a primitive instance has generic cohomology of rank at most one in degrees one and two, zero elsewhere, and $P$ spans $H^1$ when it is nonzero. Then the first line of Equation <a href="#eq:h:divisor-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:h:divisor-bounds">[eq:h:divisor-bounds]</a> holds. These hypotheses hold in every simple-zero instance and also at the base of Theorem <a href="#thm:heegner-interpolation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:heegner-interpolation">10</a>. The second line holds in genus data with irreducible $E[2]$, with a bound independent of the number of active or derivative primes.
  - Explanation: Rank-reducing switches prove nonnegative non-dyadic divisors. At the dyadic divisor, the genus estimate additionally uses residual irreducibility and the stated exceptional-field exclusions.
- **claim-uniform-residual-selmer-model-size** (bound, [source](#stmt-rl-residual-bound)): Suppose $\omega(\operatorname{disc}K)\leq A$, the local twisting classes at $2N$ belong to a fixed finite list, and all active conductor primes are split with odd Frobenius exponent of the deformation character. After localization and completion at $(2)$, the minimal free ranks of the Selmer complexes are bounded in terms of $E,A$, and the number of retained derivative primes. They do not depend on the number of active conductor primes.
  - Explanation: Bounded quadratic ramification and all-split odd deformation exponents control minimal localized model ranks independently of active conductor support.
- **claim-outer-integral-evaluation-dvr** (construction, [source](#stmt-rl-outer-evaluation)): Let $C_j$ be any family of the preceding limiting complexes, completed over $\mathcal O_j=\widehat{\Lambda_{(2)}}$, possibly for different quadratic fields $K_j$. Suppose their minimal ranks are bounded. Assume a common bounded cohomological degree interval. Keep the actual evaluation matrices and transport them to the minimal models through integral contractions. For a nonprincipal ultrafilter $\mathcal U$, put $$\mathcal O_\infty= \left(\prod_{\mathcal U}\mathcal O_j\right)/\mathfrak a, \qquad \mathfrak a=\{(x_j): \{j:v_2(x_j)\geq n\}\in\mathcal U\text{ for every }n\}.$$ Then $\mathcal O_\infty$ is a DVR with uniformizer $2$ and a characteristic-zero fraction field $L_\infty$. The outer $H^1$ over $L_\infty$ injects into crossed classes on the inner quadratic sequence group product, or its extension by one simultaneous complex conjugation for the induced representation. Its restriction to the product of their exact common kernels is injective. All arbitrary-sequence degree-two evaluation identities survive. These conclusions also hold after retaining any fixed finite collection of additional integral diagrams.
  - Explanation: A valuation-separated ultraproduct is a discrete valuation ring of characteristic-zero fraction field. Integral evaluation matrices preserve detection, exact-kernel restriction, and approximate-cycle identities through this outer limit.
- **claim-outer-induced-absolute-irreducibility** (theorem, [source](#stmt-rl-outer-irreducibility)): On the outer characteristic-zero test, $\Psi$ has infinite order and the four-dimensional representation induced from $T\chi\Psi$ is absolutely irreducible.
  - Explanation: The outer deformation retains infinite order and distinct inertia characters, while a finite Tate-matrix spanning witness preserves absolute irreducibility.
- **claim-outer-chebotarev-compatibility** (theorem, [source](#stmt-rl-outer-chebotarev)): The finite Chebotarev realization of Lemma <a href="#rl:chebotarev-evaluation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="rl:chebotarev-evaluation">83</a> is compatible with Proposition <a href="#rl:outer-evaluation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="rl:outer-evaluation">89</a> and with any fixed finite list of previous derivative operations.
  - Explanation: Finite prime realization extends through the outer evaluation construction and any fixed finite sequence of preceding derivative operations.
- **claim-compatible-inner-outer-evaluation-package** (construction, [source](#stmt-rl-limit-evaluation-package)): The finite free models, ring-class characters, local conditions and pairings constructed above can be retained simultaneously. Their inner limits have the stated height-one acyclicity and all-sequence cohomology detection. For all-split ring data with bounded $\omega(\operatorname{disc}K)$, the residual model sizes are bounded independently of the active conductor support. Their outer limits retain arbitrary evaluations, exact-kernel injectivity and finite Chebotarev realization after any fixed number of additional integral arithmetic operations.
  - Explanation: The finite models, characters, dualities, evaluations, and arithmetic target diagrams coexist in compatible inner and outer constructions with the stated support-uniform bounds.
- **claim-uniform-ring-dyadic-determinant-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-h-uniform-ring-determinant)): For simple-zero ring data with every active conductor prime split in $K$ and $\omega(k)\le a$, the coordinate of Definition <a href="#def:h:determinant-coordinate" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:h:determinant-coordinate">78</a> satisfies $$v_{(2)}(u)\ge -C_{E,a},$$ where $C_{E,a}$ is independent of $h$ and $K$. There is no residual irreducibility assumption. This is the last line of Equation <a href="#eq:h:divisor-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:h:divisor-bounds">[eq:h:divisor-bounds]</a>.
  - Explanation: All-split simple-zero ring data with bounded companion support have a uniform lower determinant valuation even without residual irreducibility.
- **claim-unused-prime-universal-correction** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-h-unused-prime-correction)): There is $\eta\in O[G]$ such that $u=\eta u_{\mathrm{rel}}$ agrees at each character with the primitive determinant coordinate up to a $\Lambda$-unit. In particular, $u_x\in\Lambda[1/2]$. If the base product derivative is zero, then $u_0(0)=0$. At the nonzero vertices, $$\label{eq:h:normalized-vertex-bound} v(u_x(0))\le B+O_{E,h_0,a}(1),$$ where $a$ bounds $\omega(k)$.
  - Explanation: An integral group-ring multiplier removes unused-prime factors characterwise. Primitive coordinates have no non-dyadic poles, vanish at a failed base derivative, and obey the punctured central upper bound.
- **claim-uniform-heegner-family-clearing** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-h-family-clearing)): For the element $u$ of Lemma <a href="#lem:h:unused-prime-correction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:h:unused-prime-correction">94</a>, there are $f,d\in O[G]$ with $d_x=f_xu_x$ at every character, $f_0\in\Lambda$, and $v(f_0(0))$ uniformly bounded. For each fixed $M$, the negative Laurent support of every $f_x\bmod2^M$ has a bound independent of $b$ and of the number of new primes.
  - Explanation: Eliminating new-prime blocks leaves a bounded old complex whose clearing factor has uniformly controlled central valuation and negative Laurent support.
- **claim-squareclass-density-conversion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-squarefree-density)): Let $\mathcal P$ be a property of nonzero signed integers unchanged by multiplication by an integer square. Suppose $$A(X)=\#\{n\in\mathbb Z:0<\|n\|\le X,\ \mathcal P(n)\} =2\delta X+o(X).$$ Then $$S(X)=\#\{d\in\mathcal D(X):\mathcal P(d)\} =\frac{2\delta}{\zeta(2)}X+o(X).$$ In particular the property has density $\delta$ among signed squarefree parameters ordered by absolute value.
  - Explanation: Square-invariant signed integer counts pass to signed squarefree counts by Möbius inversion, preserving the limiting density in the prescribed absolute-value ordering.

        "exact_quote": "There is a constant $C_E$, depending only on $E$, with the following property. Fix an odd fundamental discriminant $h_0$, prime to $2N$, with $c_2(E^{(h_0)})=0$. Assume that a constant $B$, independent of $b$, satisfies $$\\label{eq:cy:punctured-bound}\n L(E^{(h_x)},1)\\ne0,\\qquad D(h_x)\\le B\\qquad(x\\ne0).$$ If $E[2]$ is irreducible, assume also that some $L$, independent of $b$, satisfies $$\\label{eq:cy:prime-bound}\n v_2(q^2-1)\\le L\\qquad(q\\in\\mathcal Q).$$ Then $L(E^{(h_0)},1)\\ne0$ and $$\\label{eq:cy:transferred-bound}\n D(h_0)\\le B+C_E.$$ The necessary dimension may depend on $h_0$, its finite Selmer group, and the bound in Equation <a href=\"#eq:cy:prime-bound\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:cy:prime-bound\">[eq:cy:prime-bound]</a>; $C_E$ does not.",

      },

        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"prop:rough-nonvanishing\" label=\"prop:rough-nonvanishing\"></span><span id=\"nv:rough\" label=\"nv:rough\"></span>Let $E/\\mathbb Q$ have conductor $N$, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes containing the prime divisors of $2N$. For every finite set $B$ of primes there are odd fundamental discriminants $D$ of arbitrarily large absolute value such that $$\\operatorname{sign}(D)=\\sigma,\\qquad [D]_p=c_p\\quad(p\\in S),\\qquad\n p\\nmid D\\quad(p\\in B),$$ Moreover:*\n\n1.  *If $\\varepsilon=1$, they can be chosen with $L(E^{(D)},1)\\ne0$ and $\\omega(|D|)\\le5$.*\n\n2.  *If $\\varepsilon=-1$, they can be chosen with $L'(E^{(D)},1)\\ne0$, so the central zero is simple.*\n\n*The bound five in <span class=\"upright\">(i)</span> is independent of $E,S,B$ and the prescribed classes.         "anchor": "stmt-co-even",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"prop:even-coefficients\" label=\"prop:even-coefficients\"></span>Fix a nonempty filter with even functional sign. There are a holomorphic weight-$3/2$ cusp form $$g=\\sum_{n\\geq1}a(n)q^n$$ of level supported on $S$, after enlarging exponents at those primes, and finite-order characters $\\psi,\\eta$ of $2$-power order, with $\\psi/\\eta$ quadratic, having the following properties.*\n\n\n1.  *The coefficients vanish off the filter and, for $p\\notin S$, $$a(p^2n)=\\bigl(\\eta(p)a_p(E)-\\psi(p)(-n/p)\\bigr)a(n)\n                       -p\\eta(p)^2a(n/p^2).\n    \\label{cs:hecke-recurrence}$$ As usual a coefficient with a nonintegral index is zero.*\n\n\n\n2.  *After normalizing at one nonzero squarefree index, every squarefree coefficient in the filter is a rational number times a root of unity of $2$-power order. For a fixed nonzero squarefree index $D_0$, $$2v\\left(\\frac{a(D)}{a(D_0)}\\right)\n     =v\\left(\\frac{\\mathcal L(\\sigma D)}{\\mathcal L(\\sigma D_0)}\\right)\n     \\quad\\text{whenever }a(D)\\ne0.\n    \\label{cs:even-ratio}$$ Equivalently, there is a constant $c_g$, independent of $D$, such that $$2v(a(D))=v\\bigl({\\cal L}(h)\\bigr)+c_g.\n    \\label{cs:even-value}$$ In particular $a(D)\\ne0$ if and only if $L(E^{(h)},1)\\ne0$.*\n\n\n3.  *After the fixed auxiliary exclusions described below, there is a constant $C_g$ such that, at every nonzero squarefree coefficient, $$v(a(D))\\geq w(D)+\\tfrac12s(h)-C_g.\n    \\label{cs:even-lower-bound}$$ The constants depend on the fixed curve, filter and auxiliary choices, and not on $D$ or its number of prime factors.",
        "source_id": "PM-006.1"
      },

    {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-co-odd",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"prop:odd-coefficients\" label=\"prop:odd-coefficients\"></span>Assume that a constant $C_*$ satisfies $$j(P_D)\\geq w(D)+\\tfrac12s(h)-C_*\n\\label{cs:odd-bound-hypothesis}$$ for every $h$ in the filter with a simple zero. There are arbitrarily large precisions $M$, good odd primes $\\ell$ outside the fixed support, and holomorphic weight-$3/2$ forms $g_M=\\sum a_M(n)q^n$, of level supported on $S\\cup\\{\\ell\\}$, with the following properties.*\n\n\n1.  *The additional filter at $\\ell$ is $$(h_*/\\ell)=-\\sigma,\\qquad (h/\\ell)=\\sigma,\n                   \\qquad \\rho_T(\\mathop{\\mathrm{Fr}}_\\ell)\\equiv C\\pmod{2^M},\n    \\label{cs:detecting-prime}$$ where $C$ is the action of a complex conjugation. In particular $\\ell\\equiv-1\\pmod{2^M}$.*\n\n2.  *After a fixed harmless decrease in the working precision, the forms satisfy Equation <a href=\"#cs:hecke-recurrence\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"cs:hecke-recurrence\">[cs:hecke-recurrence]</a> modulo that precision, with characters $\\eta_M,\\psi_M$ of $2$-power order and quadratic ratio. Their squarefree coefficients have the form of a $2$-power phase times an integer modulo $2^M$.*\n\n\n\n3.  *If a coefficient is visible, meaning $v(a_M(D))<M$, then $E^{(h)}$ has a simple zero and $$j(P_D)\\leq v(a_M(D))+C_1.\n    \\label{cs:odd-detection}$$ For every admissible $D$ the coefficient lower bound is $$v(a_M(D))\\geq\n           \\min\\{M,\\,w(D)+\\tfrac12s(h)-C_2\\}\n    \\label{cs:odd-lower-bound}$$ when the product derivative is nonzero; if it is zero, the coefficient is zero modulo $2^M$. Here $C_1,C_2$ are independent of $\\ell,M,D$.*\n\n4.  *A fixed squarefree witness $D_w$ in the original filter is admissible at every chosen $\\ell$ and has $v(a_M(D_w))$ bounded as $M\\to\\infty$.*\n\n*For irreducible $E[2]$, the hypothesis is Theorem <a href=\"#thm:heegner-genus-bound\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:heegner-genus-bound\">13</a>.         "anchor": "stmt-tc-irreducible-rules",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose $E[2]$ is irreducible.*\n\n1.  *On matching $B_U$, coefficient $1$ of a product of root traces reads $A$ on the union of $U$ and those roots. It depends on the roots only through their total rational elementary label relative to $S\\cup U$. Any finite collection of roots, including the empty collection, may be replaced in this test by one virtual root with that label.*\n\n2.  *Changing the Legendre bit of that root against a split vertex $p$ has additive derivative equal to deletion of $p$, with its rational labels away from $p$ transferred to the total root label. Changing the root bit against a simple vertex has derivative zero.*\n\n3.  *To vary a simple vertex $q$, omit it and use opposite $B_V$, retaining the other root probes. At another simple vertex $p$, choose Frobenius lifts $g$ and $\\phi_p$ for $q$ and $p$. If their transposition images are different, the derivative under $g\\mapsto g\\tau_p$ deletes both $p$ and $q$ and transfers their rational labels to the root total. If their transposition images are equal, the derivative is zero.*\n\n4.  *In the test in (iii), variation at a split $p$ is given by the first-shell factors $c_p$ times symbols of merged configurations whose weight is one less.         "anchor": "stmt-tc-minimum-transfer",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose $E[2]$ is irreducible, and let $m$ be the least weight of an index on the filter with nonzero symbol.     {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-co-symbol-interface",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"thm:symbol-rules\" label=\"thm:symbol-rules\"></span>For either coefficient source of Propositions <a href=\"#prop:even-coefficients\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:even-coefficients\">[prop:even-coefficients]</a> and <a href=\"#prop:odd-coefficients\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:odd-coefficients\">[prop:odd-coefficients]</a>, assume its stated coefficient lower bound and use its normalized symbol and filter. Then the following rules hold for finite configurations of primes outside the level support.*\n\n1.  *With rational two-torsion, the elementary-label factorizations, contraction except in the simple–simple case, and isolation by a trivial split label are those of Proposition <a href=\"#tc:rational-rules\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"tc:rational-rules\">24</a>. A pair of identical simple labels realized with $\\#E(\\mathbf F_q)/2$ odd can be inserted without changing the symbol, as in Proposition <a href=\"#tc:simple-twins\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"tc:simple-twins\">25</a>.*\n\n2.  *With irreducible $E[2]$, all root probes combine into one total rational elementary label. A root-bit derivative at a split vertex deletes that vertex, while at a simple vertex it is zero. The derivative between two simple vertices deletes both when their transposition images are different, and is zero when they are equal. The remaining simple–split shell has weight one less. These are the rules of Proposition <a href=\"#tc:irreducible-rules\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"tc:irreducible-rules\">27</a>.*\n\n3.  *At the least weight supporting a nonzero symbol in the irreducible case, each nonroot may be moved with only its fixed-support elementary Frobenius label prescribed; internal edges impose no further condition on the value, subject to matching the total root label. This is Lemma <a href=\"#tc:minimum-transfer\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"tc:minimum-transfer\">28</a>.*\n\n*The analytic and finite-Selmer consequences of a nonzero symbol remain those of Proposition <a href=\"#prop:unit-symbol-detection\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:unit-symbol-detection\">19</a>. In the odd source the rules mean finite tests at arbitrarily high stages chosen in the ultrafilter-large sets of the prescribed stabilization.",

          "exact_quote": "<span id=\"thm:symbol-rules\" label=\"thm:symbol-rules\"></span>For either coefficient source of Propositions <a href=\"#prop:even-coefficients\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:even-coefficients\">[prop:even-coefficients]</a> and <a href=\"#prop:odd-coefficients\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:odd-coefficients\">[prop:odd-coefficients]</a>, assume its stated coefficient lower bound and use its normalized symbol and filter. These are the rules of Proposition <a href=\"#tc:irreducible-rules\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"tc:irreducible-rules\">27</a>.*\n\n3.  *At the least weight supporting a nonzero symbol in the irreducible case, each nonroot may be moved with only its fixed-support elementary Frobenius label prescribed; internal edges impose no further condition on the value, subject to matching the total root label.         "exact_quote": "Fix finitely many old vertices and individually realizable new types.         "anchor": "stmt-gr-network",
        "exact_quote": "A network satisfies $f(z,\\mathbf1)=\\mathcal N P(z)$, where $\\mathcal N$ is a sum of terminal finite-difference operators indexed by forests. In each surviving forest term, every component containing an internal primary vertex meets a terminal. A component meeting $t$ terminals has contraction degree $t-1$; a component containing two simple terminals acts as zero. Networks with disjoint internal vertices and no edges between them multiply as operators on the same $P$. In particular, degree greater than $\\deg P$ annihilates it.*\n\n\n*For the grounded Laplacian $Q$ and terminal columns $c_a$ defined above, the constant and the pair-contraction coefficients are $$\\label{gr:forest-coefficients}\n \\det Q,\\qquad c_a^{\\mathsf t}\\operatorname{adj}(Q)c_b\\quad(a\\ne b).$$ The latter multiplies the terminal difference in the selected alignment; a prohibited pair multiplies the zero operator.",

        "anchor": "stmt-pw-minimum-seeds",
        "exact_quote": "1.  *In an all-split alphabet, suppose a unit symbol has a nonempty witness. At the least positive vertex count $r$ of such a witness, all mutual edge bits are immaterial. The symbol is determined by the individual fixed-support labels. This remains true if the empty configuration is a unit, provided no contraction to the empty configuration is used.*\n\n2.  *In the quadratic case, suppose the symbol has a nonzero witness, the alphabet is closed under the allowed contractions, and it contains the good twin operations. There are $r\\ge0$ and $s_1\\ge1$ such that for every $s\\ge s_1$ of the permitted simple parity, the minimum split count of a unit with $s$ simple vertices is $r$. At these counts all edge bits are immaterial. A chosen minimum seed may be padded by arbitrarily many good twin pairs.*\n\n*The assertions also hold for a stabilized moving odd symbol, with every particular finite list of uses made at a sufficiently advanced stage.",
        "source_id": "PM-006.1"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-lm-arithmetic-realization",
        "exact_quote": "Fix finitely many individually admissible oriented prime templates, including generator neighborhoods at $S$, any additional finite places, and oriented Frobenius on $E[4]$ and fixed quadratic-radical extensions unramified outside that support. At arbitrarily fresh primes these templates admit the following simultaneous prescriptions.*\n\n1.  *Between distinct vertices, one direction of the double-coset residue bits is free and reciprocity determines the reverse direction. The available matrix blocks are all binary matrices for two split vertices in the $S_3$ case, and $J\\mathbb F_4$ in the $C_3$ case, with the rotation algebra identified with $\\mathbb F_4$. For split–simple vertices the full vector space is available, and for simple–simple vertices the scalar entry is available.*\n\n2.  *The rational Legendre bit between the absolute primes is independent of the matrix block, subject to rational reciprocity in the reverse direction.*\n\n3.  *Repeating a template fixes its simple self entry and its split self block modulo a scalar multiple of $J$. A sufficiently primary split template with trivial $E[4]$-Frobenius has self block in $\\mathbb F_2J$.*\n\n*Here *primary* means sufficiently close to $1$ at the finite places of $S$ and totally positive at the real places. New cross-bit prescriptions are made outside the support. All assertions concern finite configurations; an additional moving prime $\\ell$ may be included among the prescribed places.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-lm-address-program",
        "exact_quote": "Let $M_*$ be the singular matrix of a finite site state, and let $D$ be a sum of its pair toggles such that $N_*=M_*+D$ is invertible. For $b\\geq2$ and $0\\ne x_*\\in\\mathbb F_2^b$, one can add finitely many primary split sites, each activated by a linear form, so that:*\n\n- *all sites present in the original state have activation $l_0$, with $l_0(x_*)=1$;*\n\n- *no site is active at zero, and at $x_*$ precisely the original state $M_*$ remains;*\n\n- *the matrix is invertible at every other nonzero address;*\n\n- *the active auxiliary matrix is always invertible, and its Schur complement contributes $D$ exactly when the original sites are active and $x\\ne x_*$.*\n\n*All entries use the freedoms of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:lm:arithmetic-realization\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:lm:arithmetic-realization\">49</a>.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $D$ be a based bounded complex of finite free $O[G]$-modules, of total graded rank at most $r$, whose augmentation $D_0$ is a complex over $\\Lambda$. Let $u_x$ be the determinant tensor of their cohomology classes, with value zero in the acyclic case. In case <span class=\"upright\">(ii)</span>, take two cycles whose denominator exponents sum to at most $a_0$, suppose each constituent has pattern <span class=\"upright\">(ii)</span>, and let $u_x$ be their wedge determinant coordinate.         "anchor": "stmt-rl-finite-limits",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose diagrams of bounded finite free complexes over $A_i$, or over $A_i[G]$, have a common bounded cohomological degree interval and bounded ranks in every degree. Include the chain homotopies and inverses for every asserted identity or equivalence.         "exact_quote": "<span id=\"rl:kummer\" label=\"rl:kummer\"></span> Let $F$ be a finite extension of a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, and let $B/F$ be any elliptic curve. Put $M_F=B(F)^\\wedge_2=\\varprojlim_n B(F)/2^nB(F)$. There is a perfect local condition $$U_F=M_F[-1]\\longrightarrow R\\Gamma(F,T_2B).$$ For every $n\\geq1$, derived reduction has $$H^0(U_F\\otimes^{\\mathbf L}\\mathbf Z/2^n)=B(F)[2^n],\\qquad\n H^1(U_F\\otimes^{\\mathbf L}\\mathbf Z/2^n)=B(F)/2^nB(F).$$ Its map in degree zero is the isomorphism onto $H^0(F,B[2^n])$, and its map in degree one is the finite Kummer injection.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-h-relaxed-local",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"rl:local-acyclic\" label=\"rl:local-acyclic\"></span> For a primitive character constituent, let $C$ denote the limiting Selmer complex with full conditions at $r$ and at its active good conductor primes, and the prescribed Kummer, unramified or derivative conditions elsewhere. The limiting full local complexes are acyclic over every height-one residue field of $\\Lambda$ of characteristic zero. At $(2)$, with residue field $\\Omega=\\mathbf F_2((t))$, the $r$-complex is acyclic, as are the complexes at active split primes with odd prescribed Frobenius exponent of the deformation character and at active primes $q$ with $t_q=0$. At each of these acyclic relaxed places, the full and orthogonal strict conditions agree on the indicated test. If every relaxed place is acyclic at that test and the remaining local conditions are self-dual, global duality makes the Selmer complex self-dual. The Selmer complex has no global invariants on these tests.",

        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"rl:evaluation\" label=\"rl:evaluation\"></span> Fix $K$ and a sequence of the finite cochain constructions above. Keep the contraction maps into the original global cochains. Let $\\Gamma_K=\\prod_i G_K$ and $\\Gamma=\\Gamma_K\\rtimes\\langle\\tau\\rangle\\subset\\prod_iG_{\\mathbf Q}$, with simultaneous complex conjugation $\\tau$. Thus $\\Gamma_K$ has index two in $\\Gamma$; the larger unrestricted product of rational Galois groups is not used for induction. The matrix limit defines a coefficient action of $\\Gamma_K$ on $\\Lambda^2$. For every field $L$ receiving a map from $\\Lambda$, there is a natural injection $$H^1(C\\otimes_\\Lambda L)\\longrightarrow\n H^1_{\\rm abs}(\\Gamma_K,L^2),$$ where the right side denotes abstract crossed-homomorphism classes. Here $C$ may be the global complex or a Selmer complex whose local conditions contain all local degree-zero invariants and inject into local $H^1$. The same statement holds for the induced representation of $\\Gamma$.*\n\n*The evaluation maps and their degree-two cochain identities exist for every group sequence and commute with coefficient extension.",

        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"rd:local-model\" label=\"rd:local-model\"></span>Let a sequence of inert good primes $\\ell$ have rational Frobenius lifts tending on $T$ to a fixed complex conjugation $C_\\tau$. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Analytic rank, Mordell–Weil rank, and full Selmer corank** ([source](#sec:introduction)): Write $$a(E)=\mathop{\mathrm{ord}}_{s=1}L(E,s),\qquad r(E)=\mathop{\mathrm{rank}}_{\mathbb Z}E(\mathbb Q),\qquad c_2(E)=\mathop{\mathrm{corank}}_{\mathbb Z_2}\mathop{\mathrm{Sel}}_{2^\infty}(E/\mathbb Q).$$
- **Finite descent invariant** ([source](#pm-h-3)): Put $$d_2(E)=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}\mathop{\mathrm{Sel}}_2(E/\mathbb Q)-\dim_{\mathbb F_2}E(\mathbb Q)[2].$$
- **Valuation and finite module length** ([source](#pm-h-9)): All valuations above $2$ are normalized by $v(2)=1$, with $v(0)=+\infty$. For a finite $\mathbb Z_2$-module $M$, its length is $\log_2\#M$.
- **Local filter** ([source](#pm-h-9)): A local filter specifies a real sign and unit squareclasses at $S$ for a variable odd fundamental discriminant prime to $S$.
- **Signed prime discriminant** ([source](#pm-h-9)): For an odd prime $p$, the signed prime discriminant is $p^*=(-1/p)p$.
- **Finite Sha length** ([source](#pm-h-9)): Whenever its group is finite, write $$s(h)=\mathop{\mathrm{length}}_{\mathbb Z_2}\mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(E^{(h)}/\mathbb Q)[2^\infty].$$
- **Normalized central valuation** ([source](#eq:transfer-normalized-value)): For a twist with nonzero central value, put $$\label{eq:transfer-normalized-value} D(h)=v(\mathcal L(h))-2w(h)-s(h).$$
- **Even minimum-depth symbol** ([source](#pm-h-23)): Set $$\delta=\min_D\{v(a(D))-w(D)\},\qquad A(D)=\begin{cases} 1,&v(a(D))=\delta+w(D),\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}, \end{cases} \label{cs:even-symbol}$$
- **Stabilized odd minimum-depth symbol** ([source](#pm-h-23)): For a bounded-weight admissible sequence $\mathbf D=(D_M)$, define $$A(\mathbf D)=1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \{M:v(a_M(D_M))=\delta+w(D_M)\}\in\mathcal U,$$ and set $A(\mathbf D)=0$ otherwise.
- **Matching and opposite parity** ([source](#tc:normalized-operator)): We say that $U$ has matching parity if $\delta+w(U)$ is integral, and opposite parity otherwise.
- **Witness and partitionable graph** ([source](#stmt-gr-partitionable)): A *witness* is a finite graph with symbol $1$. A graph is *partitionable* if it admits a partition into nonempty clusters, each containing at most one simple vertex, and oriented contraction trees whose contracted graph is a witness. The contraction trees are part of the data; this definition makes no assertion about a Selmer group.
- **Primary split vertex** ([source](#pm-h-33)): A split vertex is *primary* if its generator is a square unit at every finite place of $S_F$ and positive at every real place.
- **Compatible graph projections** ([source](#pm-h-33)): We call these *compatible projections* when they forget fixed-label coordinates or take norm data, preserve primary vertices, and commute with the omitted-vertex product substitution.
- **Stationary environment** ([source](#pm-h-47)): A *stationary environment* consists of the fixed coordinates outside the variable blocks; its dimension is the number of those coordinates.
- **Site** ([source](#pm-h-48)): A *site* consists of either one split vertex or an ordered pair of simple vertices, and always supplies two matrix coordinates.
- **Ordered profile** ([source](#pm-h-51)): An *ordered profile* assigns a value to each such word, consistently with the three-state relations in each block.
- **Heegner determinant coordinate** ([source](#stmt-def-h-determinant-coordinate)): Choose an integral basis of $\det^{-1}_{\Lambda}C$. In generic rank one, the element formed by $P$ in $H^1$ and the functional $\langle P,\cdot\rangle$ on $H^2$ determines a scalar $u(C,P)\in\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda)$ in that basis. Put $u=0$ if $P=0$ or the generic rank is zero. Integral changes of determinant basis multiply $u$ by a unit.

## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-rank-and-residual-preliminaries** [claim](#stmt-pr-ranks) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pr-ranks): Kummer limits, parity, isogeny rationalization, residual subgroup classification, and the alternating Cassels–Tate pairing. -> Rank interpretation, exhaustive residual branches, and the finite-descent even defect.
- **step-local-auxiliary-nonvanishing** [claim](#stmt-nv-local-witness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-sa-interface-4): A preliminary local twist and rough nonvanishing handle even sign; a fixed-progression derivative moment handles odd sign. -> Fresh auxiliary twists in prescribed local classes, including bounded prime support in even sign.
- **step-odd-first-moment** [claim](#stmt-nv-odd-first-moment) / [proof](#proof-stmt-nv-odd-first-moment): Approximate functional equation, square-divisor separation, Poisson summation, positive zero frequency, and a power-saving nonzero-frequency estimate. -> A positive derivative first moment and arbitrarily large simple-zero witnesses.
- **step-laurent-and-schur-algebra** [claim](#stmt-lem-h-bounded-poles) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-h-bounded-poles): Integral Laurent expansions and finite geometric inverse expansions control Schur elimination. -> Pole bounds independent of the number of eliminated blocks.
- **step-finite-models-and-clearing** [claim](#stmt-lem-h-pivot-clearing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-h-pivot-clearing): Finite Artin models retain cochain maps; central elementary-divisor pivots produce polynomial clearing factors. -> A bounded clearing factor with nonzero controlled augmentation and the required cochain comparison maps.
- **step-boolean-central-transfer** [claim](#stmt-lem-h-boolean-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-h-boolean-transfer): Bound binary digit degrees, find a nonzero common congruence solution, and compare constant-term convolutions. -> Uniform punctured central valuation bounds transfer to the missing base vertex.
- **step-positive-cyclotomic-class** [claim](#stmt-lem-cy-kato-class) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cy-kato-class): Retain the real invariant line and push fixed-form Kato classes through an integral coefficient map, with smoothing and Euler corrections. -> A fixed-lattice class with uniform integral denominator, central reciprocity, and rational divisibility.
- **step-cyclotomic-specialization-and-freeness** [claim](#stmt-prop-cy-specialization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-cy-specialization): Integral Kummer conditions, local duality, and Poitou–Tate length cancellation identify the central determinant; residual concentration handles the reducible branch. -> The normalized central comparison and the reducible cyclotomic lower bound.
- **step-cyclotomic-missing-vertex** [claim](#stmt-thm-cyclotomic-interpolation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cy-cyclotomic-poles-2): Use integral residual freeness or eliminate new local blocks and clear the bounded old complex before Boolean transfer. -> Base central nonvanishing and the transferred normalized upper bound.
- **step-heegner-height-and-base-comparisons** [claim](#stmt-prop-heegner-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cy-cyclotomic-poles-3): Apply the ring-class height formula and cancel the common free-line regulator; compare quadratic Selmer groups by restriction and conjugation projections. -> Genus–ring index comparisons and sufficient uniform finite-quotient conditions.
- **step-heegner-finite-local-diagrams** [claim](#stmt-rl-finite-limits) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rl-finite-limits): Retain bounded target cochains, their contractions, integral Kummer duality, and ring-class characters with controlled local values. -> Compatible inner perfect models with the required local acyclicity and self-duality tests.
- **step-heegner-central-coordinate** [claim](#stmt-lem-h-central-valuation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-h-central-valuation): Retain the central norm relation and compute the inverse-determinant lattice using Kummer duality and Weil-restriction component factors. -> Central determinant valuation in terms of point index, Sha length, and local weights.
- **step-inner-galois-detection** [claim](#stmt-lem-h-evaluation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-h-evaluation): Retain degree-wise evaluation matrices, a finite residual detecting list, and a central-scalar argument on the exact common kernel. -> Injective specialized crossed-class detection and finite derivative-prime realizations.
- **step-integral-local-switches** [claim](#stmt-lem-h-derivative-classes) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-h-derivative-classes): Construct a split tame local model, descend once from the complete conductor with a fixed multiplier, and retain finite–singular identities and duality triangles. -> Switched derivative classes and preservation of determinant valuations without primitive localization.
- **step-height-one-reduction** [claim](#stmt-lem-h-height-one-reduction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-h-height-one-reduction): Choose detecting localizations and switch away excess test rank while retaining the generic rank-one line and determinant valuation. -> Nonnegative divisors away from the dyadic prime and the irreducible genus dyadic bound.
- **step-outer-limit-detection** [claim](#stmt-rl-outer-evaluation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rl-outer-evaluation): Bound residual model sizes, pass integral evaluation diagrams through a valuation-separated ultraproduct, and retain finite Tate spanning and prime-realization witnesses. -> Characteristic-zero outer detection and compatible finite arithmetic operations.
- **step-uniform-ring-and-genus-bounds** [claim](#stmt-lem-h-uniform-ring-determinant) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-h-uniform-ring-determinant): Contradict unbounded negative ring valuations by outer rank reduction and a bounded boundary minor, then apply normality and the central index formula. -> The genus and all-split ring lower bounds with their distinct residual hypotheses.
- **step-universal-heegner-clearing** [claim](#stmt-lem-h-family-clearing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-h-family-clearing): Correct unused-prime factors before character evaluation, eliminate new local blocks, and put all uncontrolled factors in the numerator. -> Characterwise integral rational coordinates with a uniformly controlled clearing factor.
- **step-heegner-missing-vertex** [claim](#stmt-thm-heegner-interpolation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-h-family-clearing-2): Assume the base derivative vanishes and apply central Boolean transfer above the uniform punctured valuation bound. -> A simple zero at the base product under the full stated family hypotheses.
- **step-even-and-odd-coefficient-sources** [claim](#stmt-co-even) / [proof](#proof-stmt-co-even): Use filtered Waldspurger coefficients for even sign and weighted reductions of genus Heegner sums for odd sign. -> Hecke recurrences, rational leading phases, valuation comparisons, and detecting witnesses; rational odd normalization remains conditional on its genus bound.
- **step-minimum-depth-and-unit-detection** [claim](#stmt-prop-unit-symbol-detection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-unit-symbol-detection): Minimize normalized depth, stabilize bounded-weight odd tests, and substitute unit depth into the arithmetic coefficient comparisons. -> Analytic detection and uniform central-value, point-index, Sha, and finite-Selmer bounds at unit symbols.
- **step-integral-trace-operators** [claim](#stmt-tc-shell-bound) / [proof](#proof-stmt-tc-shell-bound): Iterate exact square-index recurrences, remove the unary leading shells, and multiply by theta to obtain integral weight-two trace operators. -> Integral all-index forms, fresh-prime coefficient tests, and the characteristic-zero level identity.
- **step-residual-symbol-substitution** [claim](#stmt-co-symbol-interface) / [proof](#proof-stmt-co-symbol-interface): Combine shell bounds and the inertia identity with elementary trace quotients and the multiplicative root character. -> Finite rational and irreducible contraction, isolation, root aggregation, and minimum-weight transfer rules.
- **step-prime-graph-and-network-calculus** [claim](#stmt-gr-network) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gr-network): Realize graph bits and product templates by prime representatives, then expand finite differences over oriented forests and grounded Laplacian minors. -> Network operators with vanishing cyclic terms and exact low-degree coefficients.
- **step-simultaneous-graph-addressing** [claim](#stmt-gr-address) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gr-address): Build singular and parameterized nonsingular address programs and spend the exact ordinary top-product degree before Boolean reduction. -> Simultaneous unit evaluations for separately nonzero graph symbols at every nonzero address.
- **step-rational-seeds-and-even-converse** [claim](#stmt-pw-even-base) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pw-even-base): Stabilize minimum seeds, prepare finite reserves and neutral packets, and apply graph addressing followed by cyclotomic transfer. -> The rational even converse and the uniform partitionable-parameter estimate.
- **step-rational-odd-lower-bound** [claim](#stmt-prop-rational-odd-bound) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-rational-odd-bound): Choose bounded companions using only even estimates, then subtract the companion value from the ring-index lower bound through the genus comparison. -> The genus-index lower bound required to normalize the rational odd source without circular dependence.
- **step-rational-split-witness-and-orientations** [claim](#stmt-pw-split-witness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pw-split-witness): Use recurrence congruences and an additional integral division to obtain a nonempty split witness; correct oriented totals through conjugation coinvariants. -> A nonempty even split test and compatible orientation reserves.
- **step-rational-fixed-companion-converse** [claim](#stmt-thm-rational-converse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-rational-converse): Fix one nonvanishing companion, use compatible graph projections to make odd and even tests simultaneous, and apply fixed-field Heegner interpolation. -> The rational-two-torsion converse in both low-corank cases.
- **step-irreducible-local-matrix-interface** [claim](#stmt-prop-selmer-matrix-bound) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-selmer-matrix-bound): Realize independent residue and norm prescriptions, symmetrize the reciprocity defect by fixed types, and inject block kernels into Selmer after bounded local constraints. -> A uniform singular-block bound and tensor-linear three-state evaluations for symbols and determinants separately.
- **step-ordered-profile-saturation** [claim](#stmt-lem-sa-punctured-cube) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-sa-punctured-cube): Use finite Ramsey stabilization to retain an ordered profile, choose a maximal singular unit word, and place addressed copies with invertible path repairs. -> Finitely realizable punctured unit cubes with all sites absent at the origin.
- **step-root-calibration-and-irreducible-even-case** [claim](#stmt-lem-sa-root-calibration) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-sa-root-calibration): Prescribe linearly activated root labels and residue bits to correct support classes, split diagonals, and stationary-prime tests. -> Actual calibrated twist cubes; cyclotomic transfer settles the irreducible corank-zero case.
- **step-bounded-companion-interface** [claim](#stmt-prop-sa-bounded-companion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-sa-interface-2): Condition the even symbol by a maximal singular prefix, balance address-copy activations, and repair the remaining interface by bounded alternating updates. -> An odd unit cube with a bounded even companion, simultaneous even units, and bounded companion Sha length.
- **step-irreducible-odd-converse** [claim](#stmt-thm-irreducible-converse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-sa-interface-3): Control the varying-field base finite Selmer quotient, compare genus and ring indices, and apply Heegner transfer with the split-or-root prime alternative. -> The irreducible corank-one case, completing the irreducible converse.
- **step-unrestricted-converse-and-finite-descent** [claim](#stmt-thm-main-converse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-h-family-clearing-3): Apply the exhaustive residual dichotomy, combine both converses, and use the forward theorem; then combine finite-quotient vanishing with whole-Sha finiteness. -> The unrestricted low-corank converse and the finite-descent certificate.
- **step-squarefree-density-deduction** [claim](#stmt-thm-main-density) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-squarefree-density-2): Apply Möbius inversion to square-invariant integer counts and identify the low analytic-rank and full Selmer-corank subsets in both directions. -> The signed squarefree half-density statements and density-one rank and finiteness conclusions.

          "exact_quote": "<span id=\"prop:even-coefficients\" label=\"prop:even-coefficients\"></span>Fix a nonempty filter with even functional sign. <a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **alternating-interface-invertibility**: A symmetric invertible binary form on an even-dimensional space admits an alternating interface correction making the displayed block matrix invertible.
- **bounded-interface-map-count**: The correction can be expressed using at most the dimension of the original space many maps to the binary plane.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **singular-original-form**: Apply interface repair when the original symmetric form is singular. -> The proof that projection is injective on the block kernel requires invertibility of the original form; the repair guarantee does not extend to this input.
- **nonalternating-update**: Use the repair guarantee with an arbitrary symmetric initial correction. -> The kernel-reduction argument uses the vanishing diagonal of the alternating correction.
- **field-linear-overclaim**: Treat binary correction maps as certificates of the additional rotation-field linearity assertion. -> Binary linearity alone does not establish linearity over the rotation field.
- **finite-checks-versus-arithmetic-converse**: Interpret successful interface tests as certification of the unrestricted arithmetic converse or twist density theorem. -> The arithmetic argument also needs coefficient symbols, prime realization, local conditions, and interpolation; the finite matrix certificate covers only interface repair.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `constructive`. The binary assertion of the alternating interface repair lemma is a finite matrix construction. Its proof chooses an alternating update reducing a nonzero kernel and bounds the number of maps by the dimension of the original space. The implementation searches for such updates exactly; it does not implement the additional rotation-field linearity assertion or the arithmetic realization.

```python
# INPUTS: JSON object with square binary matrices N and D of the same size.
# PRECONDITIONS: Even size; N symmetric and invertible; D symmetric with zero diagonal.
# OUTPUTS: JSON object with maps, each a binary matrix with two rows; their pullbacks repair S(H).
# TIME: Finite exhaustive search over pairs of binary rows at each strictly increasing rank step.
# SPACE: Matrix storage and the returned correction maps.
# ARITHMETIC: Exact binary elimination; independent exact integer determinant check through sympy.
# FAILURE: Invalid input or failure to find a strictly improving update raises an exception.
import json
import sys
from itertools import product
from sympy import Matrix


def rank_binary(matrix):
    a = [row[:] for row in matrix]
    if not a:
        return 0
    r = 0
    for col in range(len(a[0])):
        pivot = next((i for i in range(r, len(a)) if a[i][col]), None)
        if pivot is None:
            continue
        a[r], a[pivot] = a[pivot], a[r]
        for i in range(len(a)):
            if i != r and a[i][col]:
                a[i] = [x ^ y for x, y in zip(a[i], a[r])]
        r += 1
        if r == len(a):
            break
    return r


def validate_matrix(a, n):
    if not isinstance(a, list) or len(a) != n:
        raise ValueError('matrix size')
    for row in a:
        if not isinstance(row, list) or len(row) != n:
            raise ValueError('row size')
        if any(type(x) is not int or x not in (0, 1) for x in row):
            raise ValueError('binary entries')
    if any(a[i][j] != a[j][i] for i in range(n) for j in range(n)):
        raise ValueError('symmetry')


def block_matrix(N, D, H):
    n = len(N)
    top = [D[i][:] + N[i][:] for i in range(n)]
    bottom = [N[i][:] + [N[i][j] ^ H[i][j] for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
    return top + bottom


def repair(N, D):
    n = len(N)
    H = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    maps = []
    current_rank = rank_binary(block_matrix(N, D, H))
    rows = list(product((0, 1), repeat=n))
    while current_rank < 2 * n:
        improved = False
        for u in rows:
            for v in rows:
                trial = [[H[i][j] ^ (u[i] & v[j]) ^ (v[i] & u[j]) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
                trial_rank = rank_binary(block_matrix(N, D, trial))
                if trial_rank > current_rank:
                    H = trial
                    current_rank = trial_rank
                    maps.append([list(u), list(v)])
                    improved = True
                    break
            if improved:
                break
        if not improved:
            raise RuntimeError('no improving alternating update')
        if len(maps) > n:
            raise RuntimeError('map bound exceeded')
    S = block_matrix(N, D, H)
    if n and int(Matrix(S).det()) % 2 != 1:
        raise RuntimeError('determinant check failed')
    return maps


obj = json.load(sys.stdin)
if not isinstance(obj, dict) or set(obj) != {'N', 'D'}:
    raise ValueError('input keys')
N = obj['N']
D = obj['D']
if not isinstance(N, list):
    raise ValueError('matrix input')
n = len(N)
validate_matrix(N, n)
validate_matrix(D, n)
if n % 2 or rank_binary(N) != n or any(D[i][i] for i in range(n)):
    raise ValueError('preconditions')
answer = repair(N, D)
print(json.dumps({'maps': answer}, separators=(',', ':')))
```

## 5. Domain engineering contracts

| domain | applies | strength | maturity | basis | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| software | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | A rank-certification component can consume a verified finite descent and rational torsion dimension, form their difference, and issue the corollary's rank and finiteness conclusions when that difference satisfies its hypothesis. Computing and certifying the descent itself remains a separate obligation. |
| games_simulation | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The arithmetic graphs encode quadratic residue tests and coefficient symbols. Their contraction operations supply no game dynamics, simulation state evolution, or physical interaction model. |
| tools | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | An arithmetic verification tool can distinguish the finite descent invariant from the full Selmer corank by retaining the finite quotient contribution. The alternating-pairing constraint justifies the low-descent certificate and prevents treating a finite quotient as proof that the original group is finite. |
| algorithms | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | The alternating interface repair gives a finite matrix construction: start with the zero correction, compute the kernel of the displayed symmetric block matrix, and add a pullback of the alternating plane form chosen to decrease its nullity. Repeating the proof's updates yields an invertible interface. |
| data_structures | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The tensor factors encode mathematical evaluations of site alternatives. The source gives no storage layout, query interface, or update-cost contract for a reusable data structure. |
| hardware_accelerators | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The Schur elimination result controls Laurent support independently of the number of blocks. This arithmetic bound supplies no accelerator architecture, memory-transfer schedule, or hardware performance guarantee. |
| crypto_security | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The pointwise converse concerns rational elliptic curves, their full Selmer coranks, and global rank and finiteness assertions. It provides no cryptographic primitive, adversary model, or security reduction. |
| machine_learning | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The ordered profile is obtained by stabilizing finitely realizable arithmetic evaluation tables. It is not a learned predictor and supplies no training procedure, loss function, or generalization guarantee. |
| optimisation_operations_research | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The maximal singular-word argument proves existence by a boundedness and saturation argument. It does not specify an optimisation problem with an effective search domain or a solver contract for finding the maximizing arithmetic word. |
| distributed_systems | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Compatibility of limiting cochain diagrams preserves algebraic identities and evaluations. It establishes no communication protocol, fault model, replication rule, or distributed consistency guarantee. |
| other (Arithmetic geometry and exact rank certification) | True | strong | adaptable | inferred | For a rational elliptic curve with an independently established low full Selmer corank, the pointwise implication certifies its analytic and Mordell–Weil ranks and whole Tate–Shafarevich finiteness. This is a conditional certificate interface; the proof does not supply a general procedure to compute its input corank. |

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-rational-base-and-low-full-corank** (hypothesis): The unrestricted pointwise converse requires a rational elliptic curve with full two-power Selmer corank zero or one. Blocked use: ['Apply the unrestricted converse to arbitrary number fields.', 'Infer rank equality or whole Tate–Shafarevich finiteness at higher Selmer corank.']
- **limit-mordell-weil-rank-is-not-full-corank** (hypothesis): A Mordell–Weil rank bound does not establish the full Selmer-corank hypothesis, which also includes the divisible Tate–Shafarevich contribution. Blocked use: ['Replace the full Selmer-corank hypothesis with the output of a rational-point search.']
- **limit-local-kummer-conditions** (hypothesis): The corank in the converse uses local Kummer conditions at every place. Blocked use: ['Apply the converse to a relaxed, strict, or otherwise modified Selmer group without establishing the required comparison.']
- **limit-finite-descent-range** (hypothesis): The finite-descent certificate requires the specified low finite descent invariant; a larger invariant does not supply the corollary's conclusions. Blocked use: ['Infer exact analytic rank or vanishing of the two-primary Tate–Shafarevich group from an arbitrary finite descent dimension.']
- **limit-finite-quotient-versus-original-group** (edge_case): Finiteness or vanishing of the quotient by the maximal divisible subgroup does not itself establish finiteness or vanishing of the original group. Blocked use: ['Treat the finite quotient of a Selmer or Tate–Shafarevich group as the entire group before the analytic implication is established.']
- **limit-density-ordering-and-finite-samples** (formal_scope): The analytic density conclusion is asymptotic in the full signed squarefree family ordered by absolute value. Blocked use: ['Require an exact half split in a finite sample.', 'Transfer the density conclusion to conductor ordering or a restricted sign or residue filter without another argument.']
- **limit-density-does-not-control-mean** (formal_scope): The density theorem alone does not determine mean analytic rank because the exceptional set may contribute to the rank-weighted average. Blocked use: ['Deduce the mean analytic-rank assertion without the separate analytic tail estimate.']
- **limit-leading-coefficient-formula** (formal_scope): Rank equality and whole-group finiteness do not supply the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer leading-coefficient formula. Blocked use: ['Claim an exact leading coefficient or an exact odd-primary Tate–Shafarevich order from the rank and finiteness assertions.']
- **limit-cyclotomic-family-uniformity** (hypothesis): Cyclotomic transfer needs families of arbitrarily large dimension, fixed sign and local classes, punctured central nonvanishing, and a valuation bound independent of dimension. The irreducible case additionally requires the stated uniform added-prime valuation bound. Blocked use: ['Transfer nonvanishing from a single finite cube.', 'Allow the punctured valuation bound or the irreducible added-prime bound to grow with dimension.']
- **limit-heegner-family-preconditions** (hypothesis): Heegner transfer requires the standing field conditions, coprimality, linear prime activations without removal of old factors, constant local classes, base corank one, and the displayed bounds independent of dimension. Blocked use: ['Invoke Heegner transfer with an uncontrolled base finite quotient or companion prime count.', 'Apply transfer when a new prime is neither split in the companion field nor of zero invariant dimension.']
- **limit-genus-and-ring-lower-bounds** (hypothesis): The genus lower bound requires residual irreducibility and a simple product zero. The ring lower bound permits arbitrary residual representation but requires every active conductor prime to split and the companion prime count to be bounded. Blocked use: ['Apply the irreducible genus bound to the rational-torsion branch.', 'Replace the all-split ring lower-bound hypothesis with the weaker split-or-root alternative used for transfer.']
- **limit-auxiliary-filter-admissibility** (hypothesis): Auxiliary nonvanishing assumes that the prescribed sign and unit squareclasses are realized by an odd fundamental discriminant with the stated functional sign. Blocked use: ['Assert a nonvanishing auxiliary twist for inconsistent local prescriptions.', 'Assign the even-sign prime-count bound to the odd-sign assertion.']
- **limit-odd-source-normalization-order** (hypothesis): The odd coefficient source requires its genus-index lower bound before minimum-depth normalization. In the rational-torsion argument that bound is established using the even source. Blocked use: ['Normalize rational odd coefficients by assuming the odd converse that the construction is intended to prove.']
- **limit-bounded-weight-precision-realization** (nonconstructive): Odd stabilized symbols use a nonprincipal ultrafilter and simultaneous actual realizations of finite bounded-weight tests; they do not provide a universal precision valid for every configuration. Blocked use: ['Exchange finite realization with an assertion at all weights at one stage.', 'Treat the stabilized odd symbol as a directly computed finite table without choosing an admissible actual stage.']
- **limit-graph-rule-and-realization-contract** (hypothesis): The graph construction depends on contraction, isolation, whole-prime omission, compatible realizable types, and the stated filter conditions. Merely having separately nonzero polynomials does not give a common unit evaluation on their original variables. Blocked use: ['Apply graph addressing to arbitrary graph-valued functions lacking the required substitution rules.', 'Omit an individual place instead of the whole rational prime.', 'Assume separately nonzero original coefficient tests already share a unit evaluation.']
- **limit-ordinary-top-product-before-boolean-reduction** (edge_case): The simultaneous-symbol degree argument multiplies top homogeneous parts before Boolean reduction so that repeated variables retain their separate contraction requirements. Blocked use: ['Impose Boolean idempotence before allocating the contraction degrees between the symbol factors.']
- **limit-symbol-determinant-identification** (formal_scope): The common site relation gives linearity of the coefficient symbol and determinant separately. Their equality requires the additional determinant-conditioned prefix construction. Blocked use: ['Identify an arbitrary coefficient symbol with its local matrix determinant from the site relation alone.']
- **limit-block-nullity-fixed-costs** (hypothesis): The Selmer lower bound from block nullities requires zero cross-block entries and fixed bounds on support types, additional constrained places, and stationary environment dimension. Blocked use: ['Sum independent block nullities when cross-block entries are nonzero.', 'Treat the comparison cost as uniform while the constrained environment grows without the stated bounds.']
- **limit-ordered-profile-is-not-permutation-invariance** (nonconstructive): The stabilized profile retains ordered state evaluations and finite arithmetic realizability; it does not assert invariance under permuting states. Blocked use: ['Permute the maximizing singular word freely.', 'Replace finite realizations by a single infinite array of arithmetic primes.']
- **limit-interface-repair-input-and-field-scope** (hypothesis): Finite interface repair requires even dimension, a symmetric invertible original form, and an alternating correction. Its rotation-field conclusion additionally requires maps linear over that field. Blocked use: ['Apply the matrix repair guarantee to a singular original form or a correction with nonzero diagonal.', 'Treat arbitrary binary maps as witnesses of the additional rotation-field assertion.', 'Use finite interface checks as a certificate of the full arithmetic converse.']
- **limit-clearing-factor-support-control** (hypothesis): Binary central transfer requires character coordinates without negative power-series terms, a nonzero central augmentation of the clearing factor, and uniform negative Laurent support at each fixed precision. Blocked use: ['Evaluate an arbitrary element of the completed localization at the center.', 'Demand or assume the same pole bound for the entire numerator or eliminated determinant factor.']
- **limit-central-cyclotomic-comparison-nonvanishing** (hypothesis): The finite valuation comparison at a corank-zero vertex applies only when its central value is nonzero. A zero central value instead gives a zero determinant specialization. Blocked use: ['Subtract infinite valuations in the central comparison.', 'Apply the finite comparison error solely from Selmer corank zero.']
- **limit-local-euler-block-at-bad-primes** (edge_case): The bad-prime localization term uses inertia cohomology, which cannot indiscriminately be replaced by twisted inertia invariants. Blocked use: ['Use the good-prime Euler-block expression at every bad reduction type.', 'Introduce an artificial central zero by substituting the wrong multiplicative-reduction local block.']
- **limit-retained-cochain-maps-and-bounded-targets** (hypothesis): Limit evaluation requires retained contractions into the original cochains, bounded target models, and compatible integral witnesses. A cohomologically equivalent replacement without those maps is insufficient. Blocked use: ['Reconstruct unrelated old complexes after derivative switches.', 'Take a bounded-model limit of the growing ring-class source without the required rank bounds.', 'Discard degree-two identities when evaluating approximate cycles through the outer limit.']
- **limit-derivative-switch-and-descent** (hypothesis): Determinant-preserving switching requires self-duality, a generic rank-one group spanned by the retained class, and nonzero finite localization. Uniform descent uses one multiplier for the complete conductor and retains every earlier singular condition. Blocked use: ['Claim determinant preservation when the next localization vanishes.', 'Replace complete-conductor descent with an accumulating primewise denominator.', 'Drop the additional precision needed for the new finite coordinate to vanish at the coefficient prime.']
- **limit-outer-ring-uniformity-scope** (nonconstructive): The unrestricted residual ring estimate uses all-split conductor data, bounded companion ramification, and a contradiction through a characteristic-zero outer limit. Bounded model ranks alone do not bound determinant valuations. Blocked use: ['Infer a uniform determinant denominator merely from a uniform complex size.', 'Extend the outer ring argument to uncontrolled companion ramification or arbitrary nonsplit conductor support.', 'Present the outer-limit existence argument as an explicit general rank or point-generator algorithm.']
- **limit-fixed-progression-analytic-uniformity** (formal_scope): The odd derivative first moment holds for each fixed admissible progression; it makes no uniformity assertion as that progression varies. Blocked use: ['Use its error estimate uniformly for a modulus or local preparation growing with the counting range.']
- **limit-squareclass-density-conversion** (hypothesis): The passage from integer counts to signed squarefree counts requires square invariance and the stated integer asymptotic. Blocked use: ['Apply the counting conversion to a property changed by multiplication by a square.', 'Infer a squarefree density without establishing the integer asymptotic.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We prove Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture: for every elliptic curve <i>E</i> over ℚ, the quadratic twists of <i>E</i> with analytic rank zero and one each have density 1/2 among signed squarefree twist parameters ordered by absolute value. We also prove the low-corank 2-converse: if the $`2^\infty`$-Selmer corank of <i>E</i> is zero or one, then it equals the analytic and Mordell–Weil ranks, and the Tate–Shafarevich group is finite.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$. Write $$a(E)=\mathop{\mathrm{ord}}_{s=1}L(E,s),\qquad r(E)=\mathop{\mathrm{rank}}_{\mathbb Z}E(\mathbb Q),\qquad
 c_2(E)=\mathop{\mathrm{corank}}_{\mathbb Z_2}\mathop{\mathrm{Sel}}_{2^\infty}(E/\mathbb Q).$$ The Selmer group uses the local Kummer conditions at every place. Its corank includes both the Mordell–Weil rank and any divisible $2$-primary contribution from the Tate–Shafarevich group. Modularity supplies the analytic continuation and functional equation of $L(E,s)$ (Breuil et al. 2001) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[BreuilConradDiamondTaylor2001](#ref-BreuilConradDiamondTaylor2001)].

<a id="stmt-thm-main-converse"></a>
<div id="thm:main-converse" class="theorem">

**Theorem 1** (The $2$-converse). *For every elliptic curve $E/\mathbb Q$ with $c_2(E)\in\{0,1\}$, $$a(E)=r(E)=c_2(E),\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(E/\mathbb Q)\text{ is finite}.$$*

</div>

There is no restriction on reduction type, complex multiplication, rational torsion, or rational isogenies. The hypothesis concerns the full $2$-power Selmer corank; a Mordell–Weil rank bound alone does not give it.

For a nonzero squarefree integer $d$, let $E^{(d)}$ denote the quadratic twist of $E$, and set $$\mathcal D(X)=\{d\in\mathbb Z:0<|d|\le X,\ d\text{ squarefree}\}.$$ Thus positive and negative parameters are counted together and ordered by absolute value. A residue class can fix the sign of the functional equation; the half-density statement below concerns the full set $\mathcal D(X)$.

<a id="stmt-thm-main-density"></a>
<div id="thm:main-density" class="theorem">

**Theorem 2** (Goldfeld’s analytic density conjecture). *For every elliptic curve $E/\mathbb Q$ and each $j\in\{0,1\}$, $$\lim_{X\to\infty}
 \frac{\#\{d\in\mathcal D(X):a(E^{(d)})=j\}}{\#\mathcal D(X)}
 =\frac12.$$ Consequently the twists of analytic rank at least two have density zero. For a density-one set of signed squarefree parameters $d$, the analytic and Mordell–Weil ranks of $E^{(d)}$ agree and its whole Tate–Shafarevich group is finite.*

</div>

The theorem follows by combining the pointwise $2$-converse with Smith’s distribution of full $2$-power Selmer coranks (Smith 2025, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[Smith2025](#ref-Smith2025)]. Section <a href="#sec:conclusions" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:conclusions">14</a> gives the deduction, including the passage from integer to squarefree parameters. The main work of this paper is the pointwise converse.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### Consequences and companion results

The converse has a finite-descent consequence. Put $$d_2(E)=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}\mathop{\mathrm{Sel}}_2(E/\mathbb Q)-\dim_{\mathbb F_2}E(\mathbb Q)[2].$$

<a id="stmt-cor-finite-descent"></a>
<div id="cor:finite-descent" class="corollary">

**Corollary 3** (A finite Selmer criterion). *If $d_2(E)\in\{0,1\}$, then $$a(E)=r(E)=c_2(E)=d_2(E),\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(E/\mathbb Q)\text{ is finite},\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(E/\mathbb Q)[2^\infty]=0.$$*

</div>

Thus a finite $2$-descent can certify the analytic rank and the vanishing of the entire $2$-primary Tate–Shafarevich group in these two cases. The proof uses the alternating Cassels–Tate pairing to pass from $d_2(E)$ to the full Selmer corank, and is given in Section <a href="#sec:conclusions" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:conclusions">14</a>.

The density theorem resolves the frequency assertion for analytic ranks zero and one. The mean analytic-rank assertion requires additional control: a set of density zero can still contribute to the rank-weighted average. The separate companion OpenAI (2026a, Theorems 1.1 and 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[OpenAIMeanAnalyticRank2026](#ref-OpenAIMeanAnalyticRank2026)] proves the required analytic tail estimate and, together with Theorem <a href="#thm:main-density" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main-density">2</a>, obtains mean analytic rank $1/2$ in the same signed squarefree ordering.

A subsequent companion (OpenAI 2026b, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[OpenAIAllPrimeSelmer2026](#ref-OpenAIAllPrimeSelmer2026)] extends the pointwise converse to every prime $p$: full $p$-power Selmer corank $r\in\{0,1\}$ forces analytic and Mordell–Weil ranks $r$ and finiteness of the whole Tate–Shafarevich group. Its proof uses the $2$-converse and analytic twist densities established here.

The rank and finiteness assertions are distinct from the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer leading-coefficient formula. The pointwise two-primary formula of OpenAI (2026c, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[OpenAITwoPrimaryBSD2026](#ref-OpenAITwoPrimaryBSD2026)], combined with the Selmer-corank densities in the proof of Theorem <a href="#thm:main-density" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main-density">2</a>, gives the exact two-primary formula on a density-one set of signed squarefree twists. Their common analytic and Mordell–Weil ranks are zero and one with density $1/2$ each. This consequence is OpenAI (2026c, Corollary 16.1) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[OpenAITwoPrimaryBSD2026](#ref-OpenAITwoPrimaryBSD2026)]; its leading-coefficient assertion concerns the valuation at $2$.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### Goldfeld’s conjecture and analytic nonvanishing

Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer’s comparisons of rational points with central $L$-values led to the conjectural equality of algebraic and analytic rank (Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer 1965) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[BirchSwinnertonDyer1965](#ref-BirchSwinnertonDyer1965)]. The conjecture also predicts finiteness of $\mathop{\mathrm{Sha}}(E/\mathbb Q)$ and a formula for the leading coefficient (Tate 1966, sec. 1, pp. 415–421) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[Tate1966](#ref-Tate1966)]. Goldfeld’s original 1979 formulation asks for the mean analytic order in a family parametrized by quadratic-field discriminants (Goldfeld 1979, 113, Conjecture (B)) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[Goldfeld1979](#ref-Goldfeld1979)]. The density formulation predicts that analytic ranks zero and one each occur half the time. Our counting convention throughout is the signed squarefree set $\mathcal D(X)$.

The analytic study of quadratic twists produced both nonzero central values and simple central zeros. Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein and Murty–Murty supplied auxiliary twists with the nonvanishing needed in Heegner-point arguments; Iwaniec and Perelli–Pomykała developed quantitative estimates for central derivatives (Bump, Friedberg, and Hoffstein 1990; Murty and Murty 1991; Iwaniec 1990; Perelli and Pomykała 1997) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[BFH1990](#ref-BFH1990), [MurtyMurty1991](#ref-MurtyMurty1991), [Iwaniec1990](#ref-Iwaniec1990), [PerelliPomykala1997](#ref-PerelliPomykala1997)]. Ono–Skinner obtained a lower bound of order $X/\log X$ for the number of nonvanishing central values among twists by fundamental discriminants $D$ with $0<|D|\le X$ (Ono and Skinner 1998, Corollary 3) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[OnoSkinner1998](#ref-OnoSkinner1998)]. More recently, Kumar–Mallesham–Sharma–Singh sharpened derivative nonvanishing estimates through second moments, and Kriz–Nordentoft improved central-value lower bounds for curves with no rational two-torsion (Kumar et al. 2024, Theorem 1) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[KumarEtAl2024](#ref-KumarEtAl2024)] <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[KrizNordentoft2025](#ref-KrizNordentoft2025)] (Kriz and Nordentoft 2025, Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.2). These quantitative results yield many twists without by themselves giving a positive proportion for every fixed curve.

Positive proportions were obtained in special families. James proved analytic-rank-zero proportions for particular curves, and Vatsal proved positive proportions of both analytic ranks zero and one for $X_0(19)$ (James 1998, Theorem 1) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[James1998](#ref-James1998)] <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[Vatsal1998](#ref-Vatsal1998)] (Vatsal 1998, Theorem II). Kriz–Li proved both positive proportions for every rational elliptic curve admitting a rational $3$-isogeny (Kriz and Li 2019, Theorem 1.5) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[KrizLi2019](#ref-KrizLi2019)]. In the congruent-number family, Tian’s Heegner-point work gives rank one and odd-order Tate–Shafarevich group in specified subfamilies (Tian 2014) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[Tian2014](#ref-Tian2014)]. Genus-period and genus-point congruences, followed by Selmer statistics, give further analytic density results (Tian, Yuan, and Zhang 2017; Smith 2016) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[TianYuanZhang2017](#ref-TianYuanZhang2017), [SmithCongruent2016](#ref-SmithCongruent2016)]. These arguments connect coefficient congruences and arithmetic statistics with analytic nonvanishing, a connection also central to the present proof.

The statistical input used here has its own progression. Smith first established higher $2$-power Selmer distributions for curves with full rational two-torsion and no rational cyclic subgroup of order four (Smith 2017) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[Smith2017](#ref-Smith2017)]. His subsequent work treated the irreducible residual case and further rational two-isogeny cases (Smith 2026a, 2026b) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[SmithDistributionI](#ref-SmithDistributionI), [SmithDistributionII](#ref-SmithDistributionII)]. The unrestricted theorem gives full Selmer coranks zero and one with density $1/2$ each for every rational elliptic curve (Smith 2025, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[Smith2025](#ref-Smith2025)]. Its analytic corollary assumes Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer (Smith 2025, Corollary 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[Smith2025](#ref-Smith2025)]. We use the Selmer theorem itself and supply the pointwise analytic implication through Theorem <a href="#thm:main-converse" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main-converse">1</a>.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### The Selmer converse problem

Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin established the forward implication: analytic rank at most one gives equality with the Mordell–Weil rank and finiteness of the whole Tate–Shafarevich group (Gross and Zagier 1986; Kolyvagin 1990) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[GrossZagier1986](#ref-GrossZagier1986), [Kolyvagin1990](#ref-Kolyvagin1990)]; see also the combined formulation in Skinner (2020, sec. 1) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[Skinner2020](#ref-Skinner2020)]. The Gross–Zagier formula relates a central derivative to the height of a Heegner point, and Kolyvagin’s derived classes control the Selmer group. A converse must produce analytic nonvanishing from Selmer information.

Cyclotomic Iwasawa theory gave rank-zero converses at good ordinary odd primes in the work of Skinner–Urban, under residual irreducibility and ramification hypotheses (Skinner and Urban 2014) <a id="pm-cite-25"></a>[[SkinnerUrban2014](#ref-SkinnerUrban2014)]. Skinner and Wei Zhang proved rank-one converse criteria through Heegner points and derived classes, under their respective reduction, residual-image and local hypotheses (Skinner 2020; Zhang 2014) <a id="pm-cite-26"></a>[[Skinner2020](#ref-Skinner2020), [Zhang2014](#ref-Zhang2014)]. Burungale–Castella–Skinner subsequently removed the auxiliary ramification conditions in the good ordinary, residually irreducible case for $p>3$ (A. A. Burungale, Castella, and Skinner 2025, Theorem 1.2.2 and the discussion following Remark 1.2.3) <a id="pm-cite-27"></a>[[BurungaleCastellaSkinner2025](#ref-BurungaleCastellaSkinner2025)]. At good supersingular primes $p>3$, Castella–Wan obtained the rank-one Selmer-corank implication for semistable curves (Castella and Wan 2024, Theorem A) <a id="pm-cite-28"></a>[[CastellaWan2024](#ref-CastellaWan2024)].

Reducible residual representations call for a different Iwasawa-theoretic comparison. Castella–Grossi–Lee–Skinner proved the corank-zero and corank-one converses at good ordinary Eisenstein primes $p>2$, with local isogeny character neither trivial nor cyclotomic (Castella et al. 2022, Theorem E) <a id="pm-cite-29"></a>[[CastellaGrossiLeeSkinner2022](#ref-CastellaGrossiLeeSkinner2022)]. Keller–Yin treated potentially good ordinary reduction at odd Eisenstein primes without that character exclusion (Keller and Yin 2024, Theorem B) <a id="pm-cite-30"></a>[[KellerYin2024](#ref-KellerYin2024)]. These results enlarge the allowed residual representations while retaining conditions on the prime and its reduction type.

The CM theory includes substantial results at the prime two. Burungale–Tian proved the rank-one converse at good ordinary primes $p>3$ (A. A. Burungale and Tian 2020) <a id="pm-cite-31"></a>[[BurungaleTian2020](#ref-BurungaleTian2020)]; Burungale–Castella–Skinner–Tian included the small ordinary primes under an additional conductor hypothesis (A. Burungale et al. 2022, Theorem A) <a id="pm-cite-32"></a>[[BurungaleCastellaSkinnerTian2022](#ref-BurungaleCastellaSkinnerTian2022)]. Ressler and Yu obtained the small-prime good-ordinary result without that conductor condition; see Yu’s Theorem 1 and the attribution in Burungale–Castella–Skinner–Tian, Remark C (Yu 2021; A. Burungale et al. 2022) <a id="pm-cite-33"></a>[[Yu2021](#ref-Yu2021), [BurungaleCastellaSkinnerTian2022](#ref-BurungaleCastellaSkinnerTian2022)]. Burungale–Skinner’s combined ordinary formulation includes $p=2$, and their good supersingular CM theorem also permits $p=2$ under an additional surjectivity condition on Selmer localization at $p$ (A. Burungale and Skinner 2024, Theorems A.3 and A.1) <a id="pm-cite-34"></a>[[BurungaleSkinner2024](#ref-BurungaleSkinner2024)].
